explain.say: Look at the roof of a warehouse or a railway shed: a pattern of triangles called a truss. Each bar only pulls or pushes along its length. Ours is a simple triangle, 4 metres wide and 2 metres high, with a 20 kilonewton load on top. By symmetry each support pushes up 10 kilonewtons.

draw.text: At each joint: ΣFx = 0 and ΣFy = 0

explain.say: Only the sloping rafter, because the tie is flat. Its upward part must be minus 10 kilonewtons, so F times sin 45 equals minus 10, giving 14.1 kilonewtons. The minus sign means it pushes into the joint: compression. Look at the arrow pointing down-left. Is the rafter being squashed or stretched?

explain.say: Squashed! Now sideways: the rafter pushes left with 14.1 times cos 45, which is 10 kilonewtons. So the flat tie must pull right with 10 kilonewtons. A pull means tension: the tie is being stretched. See the arrow to the right? What job does the tie do for the roof?

faq.q: How do I find the support reactions of a truss?
faq.a: Treat the whole truss as one rigid body and use moments and force sums. For a symmetric truss with a central load, each support takes half.

faq.q: How does the method of joints work?
faq.a: Each pin joint is in equilibrium, so you write the sum of x forces and the sum of y forces equal to zero there. Start at a joint with at most two unknown bars and work across the truss.

faq.q: How do I know if a truss member is in tension or compression?
faq.a: Assume every member pulls away from the joint, which is tension. If the answer comes out negative, the member is actually pushing into the joint, which is compression.

faq.q: Why are trusses made of triangles?
faq.a: A triangle cannot change shape unless a bar changes length, so it is rigid. A square made of pinned bars would fold flat.
A bar that carries no force under a given load. At a joint with two bars in line and a third at an angle, with no load, the third bar carries zero force.

facts: In an ideal pin-jointed truss loaded only at the joints, every member carries pure axial tension or compression.
A simple plane truss satisfies m = 2j − 3, where m is the number of members and j the number of joints.

quiz.say: At a joint, a 45 degree member must provide 20 kilonewtons of upward force. What is the force in the member?
quiz.show: A 45° member must give 20 kN upwards at a joint. Member force?

wrong.1: That multiplies by sin 45° instead of dividing.
wrong.2: Only part of a sloping force acts upwards, so it must be bigger than 20 kN.

quiz.say: Using the tension-positive convention, a member force comes out as minus 8 kilonewtons. What does that mean?
quiz.show: Tension-positive convention gives a member force of −8 kN. Meaning?
quiz.why: A negative answer means the bar pushes rather than pulls, so it is in compression.

wrong.1: Tension would come out positive under this convention.
wrong.2: Negative answers are normal; they tell you the direction.
